Navigation Map: Waypoint Dispatcher Assignment Flow

A dispatcher works two routes when handing out a job: the Dispatch Board Route, which lists every unassigned job, and the Assign Technician Route, where one job is matched to a crew member.

Assigning a job end to end is the Dispatcher Assignment Flow, a navigation flow that composes an ordered Select Job Step and aggregates a Confirm Assignment Step. The Select Job Step navigates to the Assign Technician Route once the dispatcher picks a job off the board, and it triggers the Assignment Transition, the navigation transition that carries the dispatcher between routes. The flow also aggregates the Selected Job Id, a context variable that flows to the Select Job Step so the next screen knows which job is in hand; the Select Job Step consumes that same Selected Job Id.

Because an assignment touches customer commitments, the Dispatcher Assignment Flow requires the Assignment Guard, a navigation guard. The Assignment Guard protects the Dispatch Board Route, evaluates the Dispatcher Is Authorized guard condition, and constrains the Assignment Transition so an unauthorized dispatcher cannot advance. When that condition fails, the guard triggers the Redirect To Login guard action, which navigates to the Sign In Route and depends on the Dispatcher Is Authorized condition to decide it must fire. The Dispatcher Is Authorized condition itself constrains the Assign Technician Route.

Finally, the Assignment Transition flows to the Assign Technician Route and requires the Assignment Guard before it will complete. The Selected Job Id references the Job Assignment record the dispatch backend ultimately writes.
